lessons.title: Conferences and divisions
lessons.objective: You can name how the 32 teams are grouped.

payload.prompt: Which division do the {{team|Patriots}} belong to?

diagram.alt: NFL map showing the AFC and NFC with their four divisions each.

explanation.correct: The {{team|Patriots}} are in the AFC East with Baltimore, Buffalo and Miami. They play each other twice and then 11 other AFC and NFC teams once each.
explanation.incorrect: The AFC East has four teams in the northeast. If they are the {{team|Patriots}}, this is home.
explanation.sayThisLine: AFC East. We play them twice a year.

payload.prompt: How many conferences and divisions make up the NFL?
payload.template: The NFL has {{conf}} conferences with {{div}} divisions each, and {{teams}} teams per division.

explanation.correct: Two conferences (AFC and NFC), four divisions in each (East, West, North, South), four teams in each division. That is 32 teams total.
explanation.incorrect: Two conferences, four divisions per conference, four teams per division. 2 × 4 × 4 = 32.

payload.prompt: How many games does each team play in a season?

options.text: 14 games over 16 weeks
17 games over 18 weeks with a bye
16 games over 17 weeks

explanation.correct: Seventeen games over 18 weeks, with one bye week off to rest and heal. That bye is scheduled differently for each team to keep games spread across the season.
explanation.incorrect: Since 2021 the regular season has been 17 games. You play them over 18 weeks because one of those weeks is your bye week.

statement.speaker: Fan
statement.text: Do not start anyone on bye. Check the schedule.

payload.question: What is she worried about?

options.text: Players who play on their team's bye week might not show up
Her fantasy players will not score if their real team does not play that week
The bye week means the season is over
Bye weeks are when players get injured

payload.translation: In fantasy, your players score points from their real games. If their actual team has the bye week off, they score zero that week, so you need a backup.

followUps.line: When is your team's bye week?
followUps.why: Tests whether you know bye weeks are scheduled and matter to fantasy planning.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Bye weeks are the simplest thing about fantasy. If the real team does not play, the real player does not score. Plan for it.

lessons.title: Making the playoffs
lessons.objective: You can explain seeds, wild cards and the bye.

payload.prompt: Put the path to the Super Bowl in order.

items.why: Seven teams per conference make it: four division winners plus three wild cards. The wild cards play each other first.
The division winners rest while wild cards play. In the divisional round, the number-one seed plays the wild-card winner.
The last four standing from your conference face off in the divisional round. Two winners go to the conference championship.
The AFC and NFC champions meet for the title. This is the goal for every team on January 1.

explanation.correct: Wild card rounds are first (wild cards vs each other, number one seed waits). Then divisional (number one plays the wild-card winner), then the conference championship, then the Super Bowl.
explanation.incorrect: The bracket works from 14 teams down to one champion. Wild card is first, divisional is second, conference championship is third, Super Bowl is fourth.

payload.prompt: Why do teams want the number-one seed?

options.text: It is the only team that gets a first-round bye
The number-one seed always wins
Only the number one seed plays at home

explanation.correct: Only the number-one seed gets a first-round bye. That is a full week to rest and prepare while the wild cards burn energy. In the playoffs, rest is gold.
explanation.incorrect: The number-one seed skips the wild card round and goes straight to the divisional playoffs. While teams 2-7 play each other, the one seed rests.

payload.prompt: How many wild-card teams make the playoffs from each conference?

diagram.alt: NFL playoff bracket showing seven teams per conference: four division winners and three wild cards.

explanation.correct: Three wild-card teams per conference, plus four division winners, makes seven playoff teams total from each conference.
explanation.incorrect: Wild cards are the next-best teams who did not win their division. Three get in from each conference (NFC and AFC).
explanation.sayThisLine: Three wild cards per conference, plus the four division winners.

payload.prompt: How many teams make the NFL playoffs?
payload.template: {{num}} teams per conference make the playoffs, for a total of {{total}} in the postseason.

explanation.correct: Seven from the AFC and seven from the NFC: four division winners and three wild cards each. Seven plus seven is 14 total.
explanation.incorrect: Seven teams per conference (four winners plus three wild cards) means 14 teams in the playoff hunt.

lessons.title: The draft
lessons.objective: You can say why bad teams pick first.

payload.prompt: Why does the team with the worst record pick first in the draft?

options.text: To give them the best chance to improve and stay competitive
As a punishment for losing so much
Because they earned it

explanation.correct: The draft is designed so bad teams get help improving. The worst team picks first and gets first pick of college talent, trying to balance talent across the league so every team can compete.
explanation.incorrect: Losing gets you the first pick because you need the most help. It is a chance to find a star and turn things around, not a punishment.

statement.speaker: Coach
statement.text: The draft is in April, right when spring practice should be going.

payload.question: What is he explaining?

options.text: The timing of the draft interferes with his team's training
April is the best month for football
Spring practice is not important
The draft should be in the fall

payload.translation: The NFL Draft happens every April, and it falls right in the middle of the spring when college coaches are developing players. It is a scheduling conflict coaches complain about.

followUps.line: When is the draft in your country or league?
followUps.why: Tests whether you know the draft is a real event with a real date.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: The draft is simple: one day a year in April, 32 teams pick college players in order, worst team first.

payload.prompt: Match the draft term to its meaning.

pairs.definition: Each selection phase of the draft; there are seven rounds, so teams pick seven players.
The order in which a team selects. If you have the first pick, you choose before anyone else.
After the draft, a ranking of players at each position showing starters and backups.

explanation.summary: Rounds are phases (1-7). Picks are the order within each round. The depth chart shows who is first on the team at each spot.

payload.prompt: How many rounds does the NFL Draft have?

options.text: Three rounds
Five rounds
Seven rounds

explanation.correct: Seven rounds, so each team gets to pick seven players total. The first few rounds are televised live; later rounds go quicker.
explanation.incorrect: The draft is seven rounds long. Day 1 is rounds 1-3 (the big stars). Day 2 is rounds 4-5. Day 3 is rounds 6-7 (role players).

lessons.title: The salary cap
lessons.objective: You can say why teams cut good players.

payload.prompt: Your star defensive end is too expensive. Keep or cut?

situation.narrative: You are $15 million over the salary cap. Your elite pass rusher makes $20 million this year. Free agency starts in three weeks.

options.label: Keep him and find other cuts
options.consequence: You are still over the cap and have to make more cuts. Those cuts might be younger, cheaper players with potential.
considerations: You cannot kick the cap problem down the road

options.label: Cut him and free up cap space
options.consequence: You save $20 million and get under the cap. He hits free agency and probably signs with a playoff team. You lose elite production but fix the math.
considerations: The cap is real; you have to balance talent and money

payload.expertNote: The salary cap is not optional. Teams make these painful cuts every year. It is why you see star players traded or cut; the cap forces hard choices.

payload.prompt: What is the salary cap?

options.text: The total amount each team can spend on player salaries each year
The maximum salary any single player can make
A tax the league collects from rich teams

explanation.correct: The salary cap is a league-wide limit: all 32 teams have roughly the same amount to spend. It is why teams have to cut good players—the math does not work anymore.
explanation.incorrect: Every team has a cap number set by the league. If you are over it, you must cut players or the league penalizes you. It creates parity.

statement.speaker: GM
statement.text: We are cap-strapped. I have to make hard choices about who to keep.

payload.question: What is she saying?

options.text: The team's hats and visors are bad
The team is close to or over the salary cap and has to cut players
The team's stadium is full
The team is too young to win

payload.translation: Cap-strapped means spending so much on existing contracts that there is no room to sign new players or give raises. It forces tough roster decisions.

followUps.line: Why would being cap-strapped force a team to cut a good player?
followUps.why: Tests whether you understand the cap limit and trade-offs.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: The cap is just math. Too much money on the books means you have to cut someone to fit under the limit.

payload.prompt: Match the cap term to its meaning.

pairs.definition: The league-set spending limit each team has for player salaries in a year.
When contracts end and players can sign with any team, usually in March.
A tool to keep a star player for one more year before free agency, paying him a high salary.

explanation.summary: The cap limits spending. Free agency lets players leave if they want. The franchise tag is one last way to keep a star.

lessons.title: Rosters and injuries
lessons.objective: You can decode roster moves in the news.

payload.prompt: Match the roster spot to what it means.

pairs.definition: The active roster: 53 players who are eligible to play in games.
Extra players who practice with the team but cannot play in games unless called up.
A list for injured players out for weeks or the season; frees up an active roster spot.

explanation.summary: The active roster is who plays. The practice squad are backups waiting. IR is for injured players who free up space.

statement.speaker: Analyst
statement.text: He is on injured reserve for the season. You can write him off.

payload.question: What does that mean for his team?

options.text: He will miss a few games but come back
He will not play at all this year; his roster spot can be used elsewhere
He is playing but hiding an injury
He is being punished for poor play

payload.translation: Injured reserve is the formal list for players too hurt to play. They are gone for the season, and the team can replace them on the active roster with a healthy player.

followUps.line: How long is an IR stint usually?
followUps.why: Tests whether you know IR is for long-term injuries, not a sprain that heals in two weeks.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: IR is simple: if a player goes on injured reserve, he is out for weeks or the year. Check the injury report each week to see who is healthy.

payload.prompt: How many players are on a team's active roster?

options.text: 32 players
48 players
53 players

explanation.correct: Fifty-three players on the active roster, though only 48 dress for a game. The other five are healthy scratches or backups.
explanation.incorrect: The 53-man roster is the limit after roster cuts in training camp. It is a key date every August.

payload.prompt: Teams manage multiple roster types to build depth.
payload.template: The {{active}} roster plays in games. The {{ps}} practices but cannot play unless called up. Injured reserve {{ir}} freed up a spot when a player was hurt.

explanation.correct: The 53-man is the main team. Practice squad waits for a shot. IR takes injured players off the active roster so you can use that spot.
explanation.incorrect: The main active team has 53 players. The practice squad is extras. When someone gets hurt, they go on injured reserve and free up a spot.

lessons.title: Trades and deadlines
lessons.objective: You can say what a trade means for a team.

payload.prompt: Why would a team trade a star player to another team?

options.text: To get draft picks or future help when they are rebuilding
To be nice to the other team
Because they have to by league rule

explanation.correct: When a team is out of the playoff race, they sell star players for draft picks and young talent. Those picks help them rebuild for the future.
explanation.incorrect: A trade is a business move. A team gives up a good player now for assets (picks, prospects) to help later when they rebuild.

payload.prompt: Your team is 3-9 and out of it. Trade your best receiver for picks?

situation.narrative: It is November 5th, just before the trade deadline on November 12th. You are hopeless for the playoffs. A playoff team offers two draft picks for your star.

options.label: Make the deal and get picks
options.consequence: You collect draft picks to rebuild. The receiver helps a playoff team now. You are worse this year but better in years 2-3.
considerations: The receiver's last years are wasted on a bad team

options.label: Keep him and finish the season
options.consequence: You play out a lost season with him. Next year he costs money and you still lose. You traded nothing and gained nothing.
considerations: Losing is not loyalty; it is wasting time

payload.expertNote: Trade deadlines separate buyers (trying to win now) from sellers (rebuilding). The best rebuilds happen when a seller admits it and gets picks.

statement.speaker: Reporter
statement.text: The trade deadline passed. Teams are locked in now.

payload.question: What just happened?

options.text: No more trades are allowed until the off-season
All trades are now free
The season is over
Teams have to fire their coaches

payload.translation: The trade deadline is a date (early November) after which teams cannot trade until the off-season. It forces teams to make a choice: buy (if you are close to winning) or sell (if you are out).

followUps.why: Tests whether you know deadlines are real dates that matter.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Trade deadline is the line in the sand. Before it, teams deal. After it, nobody can move until the next year.

payload.prompt: Match the trade term to what happens.

pairs.definition: The date after which no trades are allowed until the off-season.
A team near the playoffs that trades for a star to help them win now.
A team out of the race that trades stars for draft picks and prospects.

explanation.summary: The deadline is November. Buyers add talent to win now. Sellers trade away talent to rebuild in the future.

lessons.title: Fantasy football
lessons.objective: You can follow a fantasy conversation without panic.

statement.speaker: Friend
statement.text: I just used my number-two waiver pickup on a running back off the bench.

payload.question: What is she doing?

options.text: She is replacing her injured starter with a backup from free agency
She is ranked second in the league overall
She is breaking the rules
She is quitting fantasy

payload.translation: In fantasy, waiver priority goes to lower-scoring teams so they can pick up free players. She burned a high priority on a backup, so she must have had an injury or bye-week crisis.

followUps.line: Did she make a good move?
followUps.why: Tests whether you know bye weeks and injuries create emergencies in fantasy.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Fantasy is just your draft picks plus free-agent pickups (waivers). When someone gets hurt, you grab his backup on waivers.

payload.prompt: Match the fantasy term to what it is.

pairs.definition: At the start of the season, you pick real players in order to build your team.
When your player's real team does not play, he scores zero points for you.
Grabbing a free player from the pool of unowned players to replace someone who is hurt or on bye.

explanation.summary: Draft to start. Bye weeks happen every week (different players rest). Waivers are how you fix problems mid-season.

payload.prompt: What is the goal of fantasy football?

options.text: Score the most points by collecting real players and using their real stats each week
Predict the Super Bowl winner
Learn all the rules of the sport

explanation.correct: You draft real players and score points from their real stats each week. Touchdowns, receiving yards, tackles—it all adds up. High score wins.
explanation.incorrect: Fantasy is a game where real players score you real points. It runs from September to January, one week at a time.

payload.prompt: Smart fantasy managers plan ahead.
payload.template: Do not draft {{avoid}} during the same week. Check {{check}} before setting your lineup. A {{problem}} ruins a week if you forget.

options: players on the same bye week
gaps.correct: players on the same bye week

explanation.correct: If three of your starters are on bye the same week, you have no one to start. Check who is injured before Sunday. Bad planning costs wins.
explanation.incorrect: Do not draft multiple starters with the same bye week, or you lose them all at once. Check injuries before Sunday games, and plan for bye weeks.

lessons.title: Game day life
lessons.objective: You can talk primetime, tailgating and Super Bowl Sunday.

statement.speaker: Fan
statement.text: Our game is Sunday Night Football. The whole country will watch.

payload.question: Why does that matter to her?

options.text: Sunday Night Football is always the worst game
Prime-time games get the most viewers and the spotlight
Sunday Night Football means her team will lose
She cannot watch if it is in prime time

payload.translation: Prime-time games (Thursday, Sunday and Monday night) are nationally televised with big audiences. It is a stage and a chance for her team to shine nationally.

followUps.line: What are the three prime-time slots in the NFL?
followUps.why: Tests whether you know the schedule structure.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Prime time just means 'on national TV at night.' Thursday Night Football, Sunday Night Football, Monday Night Football. Big stage.

payload.title: Tailgate day plans
payload.setting: Text from a friend the morning of a big home game.

exchanges.theirMessage: Tailgate at my place today? We are grilling, lots of people coming.

replies.text: Absolutely! What time should I get there?
replies.coachNote: Enthusiasm and asking the practical question.

replies.text: Let me see if I can make it.
replies.coachNote: Hedging loses momentum. Just say yes or no.
She invited you. Save the opinion for later.

exchanges.theirMessage: Bring something for the grill or a drink. Nothing crazy, just join in.

replies.text: I will bring burgers and some beer. Sound good?
replies.coachNote: Specific contribution and asking, not assuming.
Vague. Be specific so she does not have to follow up.

replies.text: I am just coming to watch the game.
replies.theirResponse: If everyone did that, no one eats.
replies.coachNote: Tailgate is communal. Everyone pitches in.

payload.closingNote: Tailgating is the ritual. Food, friends, and the game after. It is as much about the culture as the sport.

payload.prompt: When is the Super Bowl played?

options.text: In December, the week after the regular season ends
In February, after the playoffs
In January, on New Year's Day

explanation.correct: The Super Bowl is in February (usually the first Sunday after February 1). The playoffs run in January, so the championship is early in the new year.
explanation.incorrect: Super Bowl Sunday is a national holiday for football fans, usually the first Sunday in February. It is the climax of the season.

payload.prompt: Game day is built into the culture.
payload.template: {{primetime}} games are on national television. The {{superbowl}} is the biggest game, played each {{month}}.

explanation.correct: Thursday, Sunday and Monday night prime-time games get the big audiences. The Super Bowl is the finale, in early February, and it is an unofficial national holiday.
explanation.incorrect: Thursday Night Football, Sunday Night Football, and Monday Night Football are the prime-time slots with huge viewership. The Super Bowl is the championship, always in February.
